names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 24 Μαΐου, which names the whole company, and out of the life page's own head line for him or her; the rank words are left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 24. мај ст. ст., „Свети мученици Мелетије стратилат и хиљаду двесто осамнаест војника са женама и децом“ — Свети is not a rank, мученици is the `martyr` this corpus puts in `types`, стратилат is the `soldier` it puts there too, and everything after „и“ is the unenumerated company and not part of his name. Strip all of it and the bare personal name is what the calendar gives. **The fold was measured on both instruments, not assumed**: `foldchk.py` compares the stored string exactly and returns `NO FOLDER HOLDS THIS FORM` for «Мелетије», so this is the first folder to hold that form — but `corpus-gate.mjs` folds on a looser reading of the name and its «мелетије» row now reads `meletius-of-antioch, meletius-the-stratelates`, so on the gate’s reading it **is** a joining, of two. The two instruments answer different questions and both answers are recorded here rather than the first one alone. The Greek form on this folder, «Μελέτιος», is the same bare name.

The heading of the calendar’s name link 1508, «Мелетий Галатийский, трибун, мч.», with the two rank words after the comma left off. THE RANK WORD IT GIVES IS NOT THE LINE’S: the day line calls him «Мелетия Стратилата», commander, and the life «военачальником Галатийской области», while the name page calls him трибун, tribune, which is the grade of the twelve whose names the same life lists separately. The link is reached from the word «Мелетия» in the line’s «Мелетия Стратилата» and so is this man’s; the discrepancy is the calendar’s and is reported to the author. `fk.mjs` returned NONE for «Мелетий Галатийский» before the write, and the form was stored on this folder only, not on `meletius-of-the-twelve-tribunes`.

death.note: Widened, not narrowed, because two books disagree by a century. saint.gr gave „between 218 and 222“, which this folder held alone. Охридски пролог за 06.06.2026 (24. мај ст. ст.): „Оптужен … у време цара Антонина“ and „Сви чесно пострадаше у II веку и преселише се у царство Христа Бога“. The century is stated and not derived from the reign, and no attempt is made to say which Antoninus the Prologue means.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 24 мая ст. ст. — «Мчч. Мелетия Стратилата, Стефана , Иоанна , Серапиона египтянина, Каллиника волхва, Феодора и Фавста , и с ними 1218 воинов с женами и детьми (ок. 218).»

attestations.note: He is the head of the day’s company and the line names him by the title this folder’s display name carries, «Мелетия Стратилата». The calendar’s life, life1135, makes him «военачальником Галатийской области» under «римского императора Антонина Гелиогобала (218–222)», a Christian who prayed that the Lord would end the pagan error; the demons of the temples, frightened by his prayer, went into dogs whose howling terrified the province; he destroyed the maddened dogs and the shrines with his soldiers, was taken before the governor Максимиан, was tortured for refusing to sacrifice and died confessing Christ. `dates` IS UNCHANGED: the folder holds «101–200 or 218–222», widened by an earlier reading, and the Russian gives the reign 218 to 222 and the line «(ок. 218)», which fall inside it. THE CALENDAR KEEPS ONE NAME PAGE WHERE THIS CORPUS KEEPS TWO FOLDERS, AND THE AUTHOR SHOULD SEE IT: name page 1508, reached from the word «Мелетия» inside «Мелетия Стратилата», is headed «Мелетий Галатийский, трибун, мч.» — tribune, not stratelates — while the same life page lists among the twelve tribunes a second «Мелетий». This corpus holds `meletius-the-stratelates` and `meletius-of-the-twelve-tribunes` as two folders. The form was stored on THIS folder, the one the line names, and on no other; the other folder’s row says the same thing from its side. azbyka.ru was not read.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (30 September 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 24ης Μαΐου — «Άγιος Μελέτιος ο στρατηλάτης και οι συν αυτώ Μάρτυρες Ιωάννης, Στέφανος, Σεραπίων ο Aιγύπτιος, Καλλίνικος ο μάγος, Μαρκιανή, Παλλαδία, και Σωσάννη, Κυριάκος και Χριστιανός τα Νήπια, δώδεκα κομήτες και τριβούνοι, Φήστος, Φαύστος, Μάρκελλος, Θεόδωρος, Μελέτιος, Σέργιος, Μαρκελλίνος, Φήλιξ, Φωτεινός, Θεοδωρίσκος, Μερκούριος και Δίδυμος, καθώς και άλλοι έντεκα χιλιάδες διακόσιοι οκτώ Μάρτυρες»

attestations.note: **The company is enumerated and is therefore one folder per named member.** The life page carries a separate head line for each of twenty-two people — Μελέτιος ο Στρατηλάτης, Ιωάννης, Στέφανος, Καλλίνικος ο Μάγος, Μαρκιανή, Σωσάννη, Κυριάκος τὸ Νήπιον, Χριστιανός τὸ Νήπιον, Παλλαδία, Σεραπίων ο Αιγύπτιος, and the twelve komites and tribunes Φήστος, Φαύστος, Μάρκελλος, Θεόδωρος, Μελέτιος, Σέργιος, Μαρκελλίνος, Φήλιξ, Φωτεινός, Θεοδωρίσκος, Μερκούριος, Δίδυμος — so twenty-two are named and twenty are drafted, because the corpus already keeps `serapion-martyr-24-may` and `marciana-martyr-24-may` on this same day from doxologia.ro's bare lines and those two are upgrades. **The eleven thousand two hundred and eight are not named and are no folders**, and are left out and reported. No hymn is printed for any of them. His own head line reads «Αγιος Μελετιος ο Στρατηλατης» and the page calls him «ο αρχηγός ας πούμε της μαρτυρικής αυτής σειράς», the leader of this line of martyrs. **He is none of the many Meletii the corpus keeps** — of Antioch, of Kharkov, the New of Myoupolis, of Cyprus, of Ryazan, of Lardos, of Stânișoara and the rest — all of whom are on other days; the sweep proposed them on the bare name. The page has him hanged, «τον μεν Μελέτιο απαγχόνισαν», and his couplet turns the pine he hung on into honey.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 06.06.2026 (24. мај ст. ст.) — „Свети мученици Мелетије стратилат и хиљаду двесто осамнаест војника са женама и децом“

attestations.note: The day’s second entry, on the same menologion 24/5 the Greek row already carries. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as all three of this day’s and all three of the 23 May’s do. **A COMPANY THAT ENUMERATES NOBODY, SO IT IS ONE ENTRY.** The heading counts his men — „хиљаду двесто осамнаест војника са женама и децом“, one thousand two hundred and eighteen soldiers with their wives and children — **and names not one of them**, and the body names nobody either. By BRIEF.md §4’s ruling a company that enumerates its members is one folder per member and one that names nobody is one entry, so **this is one row on this folder and nothing else**. The number is new: saint.gr’s heading says only „και οι συν αυτώ Μάρτυρες“. **The twenty-one folders this folder already relates to — the twelve tribunes, the two infants, the three women, Callinicus the magus and the rest — come off saint.gr’s life and not off this heading, and not one of them gains a row from this book**, which does not name them. **THE DEATH IS WIDENED, AND THE TWO BOOKS ARE A CENTURY APART.** This folder holds `death` 218 to 222 off saint.gr, „between 218 and 222“. The Prologue says the suffering was **in the second century** — „Сви чесно пострадаше у II веку“ — and names the emperor as **Антонин**. A century stated outright is not a derivation from a reign, so it is usable; and this corpus **widens where two books disagree and refuses to narrow**, so `death` becomes `earliest` 101, `latest` 222 with the display `101–200 or 218–222`, which holds both readings and asserts neither. **The dash form is deliberate**: `286–305 or about 308` reads in both languages where `between 286 and 305, or about 308` fails `lives.test.mjs` with `cannot read`, so the compound is written with dashes throughout. **121 years, so it is under `date-audit`’s 150-year `wide` threshold and the finding does not move.** **And no attempt was made to say which Antoninus is meant** — that is exactly the identification this corpus does not make from a name, and it is why the interval and not a choice is what got written. **New here**: that he was **accused of destroying a heathen temple**, which saint.gr does not give as the charge; and that **he was nailed to a tree and gave up his holy soul so**, „Прикован за дрво, Мелетије испусти своју свету душу“. The Prologue confirms `martyr` and `soldier`: „стратилат“, and the soldiers who were under his command and would not deny Christ their Lord. **No new types**, the folder holding both already. **The emperor Антонин gains nothing** by the coordinator’s third ruling: no calendar read for this corpus keeps him, and he is not a saint. No `locations`, the entry naming no place at all. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
